title: Calculation Shortcut Mastery
tagline: Year 4 — Digital roots, successive percentages a + b + ab/100, rule of 72, divisibility tests and quick LCM/HCF checks

introduction.overview: Beyond everyday mental methods there is a set of exact shortcuts that apply to whole classes of aptitude problems: the successive-change formula a + b + ab/100, the digital-root check for products, the rule of 72 for doubling time, divisibility tests for 3, 4, 8, 9 and 11, and quick LCM/HCF tricks. These are worth learning precisely because they apply to many question types.
introduction.placementRelevance: Percent change, compound growth, divisibility and LCM questions appear in most aptitude papers; shortcuts cut each to a few seconds.
introduction.realWorldContext: Quick checks catch arithmetic slips in any calculation.

learningObjectives: Use a + b + ab/100 for successive changes
Estimate doubling time with the rule of 72

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Net change after +a% and +b%: a + b + ab/100 percent.

coreDefinitions: Digital root: repeated digit sum of a number.
Divisibility test: a quick rule to check a divisor.
Successive change: changes applied one after another.
HCF × LCM = product of two numbers.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Many exact results can be produced or checked from the digits alone.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: For percent changes use the formula; for checks use digital roots; for divisibility use the test.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Digital root check
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Root of product = root of product of roots

mainNarrative: At 8% growth money doubles in about 72 ÷ 8 = 9 years.
2,376: digit sum 18, so divisible by 9; 2,376 ÷ 11? alternating sum 2 − 3 + 7 − 6 = 0, so divisible by 11.
HCF of 12 and 18 is 6, so LCM = 12 × 18 ÷ 6 = 36.

deepDiveAspects.title: Successive discounts
deepDiveAspects.content: Discounts of 20% and 10% give 20 + 10 − 2 = 28% net discount.

deepDiveAspects.title: Digital roots catch most slips
deepDiveAspects.content: They fail only for errors that are multiples of 9.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: A failed root check kills an option.
